replies:
Good — final round prep for Lincoln International analyst. Below is a focused, timed plan and exactly what to practice now (I assumed a 60–90 minute final with technical and behavioral questions). After you do or answer any item, send one answer back and I’ll score and rewrite it.
1) Quick game plan (what interviewers expect)
- Clear 60s intro: background → why banking/M&A → what you bring (modeling, accounting, attention to detail) → closing line: why Lincoln International.
- Three STAR stories: team win, hard quantitative problem, a failure + what you learned — each 40–60s and with a measurable outcome.
- Technicals: accounting (working capital, cash vs. accrual, revenue recognition adjustments), valuation (walk through a DCF, comps vs. precedent transactions), and deal mechanics (LBO basics, purchase price adjustments, synergies).
- Ask 2 smart questions about the team and deal flow.
2) Write your 60-second "Tell me about yourself"
Use this template and fill in your facts:
- Sentence 1 (background): “[University/role and years], focused on [finance/accounting/modeling], most recently [current role/title at Company].”
- Sentence 2 (skills & experience): “I’ve completed [X] financial models, [types of deals or projects], and become strong at [skill — e.g., three-statement modeling, Excel, valuation].”
- Sentence 3 (why banking/M&A): “I enjoy [synthesizing financial analysis + client work], and M&A lets me [impact/outcome you like].”
- Sentence 4 (why Lincoln): “Lincoln’s focus on [middle-market / sector / global cross-border — pick from their site or recruiter’s note] and hands-on deal execution fits my experience and the type of deal exposure I want.”
Example (edit to your facts): “I graduated from [school] and worked two years as a [role] at [firm] where I built 10+ three-statement and transaction models. I’m strongest at identifying key drivers, building clean DCF and merger models, and presenting results to stakeholders. I’m pursuing M&A because I want direct deal exposure and to work on complex cross-border transactions. Lincoln’s middle-market focus and sector expertise in [X] is the right fit for the kind of hands-on deal work I want to do.”

Practice: say it out loud and time it to 50–70 seconds.
3) Three behavioral stories — pick and structure now
Write one-sentence prompts for each, then expand to CAR/STAR:
- Team win: situation, your action (what you did), result with number (revenue saved, time saved, error reduced).
- Hard problem: a modeling or accounting trick you solved; show steps and a quantitative result.
- Failure: brief situation, your responsibility, what you changed, measurable improvement after.
Send your three one-sentence prompts and I’ll turn each into a 40–60s polished answer.
4) Technical checklist + practice questions (speak answers, 90–120s each)
Practice these exact prompts aloud:
- Accounting: “Walk me through the three financial statements. How does an increase in AR affect cash flow?” (Answer: net income down/up? show short link from IS → BS → CF.)
- Valuation: “How do you build a DCF? What are the main sensitivities?” (Cover free cash flow, WACC, terminal value; show why growth and WACC move value.)
- Deal mechanics: “What’s an LBO? How does leverage affect return to equity?” (Cover purchase price, financing, covenants, IRR drivers.)
- Market comps vs. precedent transactions: “Why do transaction multiples differ from trading multiples?”
I’ll score your spoken answers when you send them.

5) Technical quick facts to memorize (say them now, then I’ll quiz)
- Free cash flow = EBIT*(1 - tax) + D&A - CapEx - ΔNWC
- WACC = (E/V)*Re + (D/V)*Rd*(1 - tax)
- Terminal value: Gordon Growth = Final Year FCF*(1+g)/(WACC - g)
- Working capital: ΔNWC = ΔCurrent Assets (ex cash) - ΔCurrent Liabilities (ex debt)
- Goodwill = Purchase price - Net tangible assets (fair value)
6) Two questions you should ask them (short, to show deal interest)
- “Can you describe the typical deal team structure for an analyst on live transactions and what responsibilities analysts own from day one?”
- “What types of recent deals or sectors are you most active in, and where do you expect deal flow to grow over the next 12 months?”

7) Logistics + final checklist (confirm these with recruiter)
- Exact interview time, time zone, link or address, names and roles of interviewers.
- Bring a printed one-page resume, a pen, and a paper with your 3 stories and 2 questions.
- Test your camera/mic and internet 30–60 minutes before.
What I’ll do next when you send me one thing:
- Send me your 60s Tell Me About Yourself and I’ll rewrite it tighter and score it.
- Or send one technical answer and I’ll score it and give one concrete fix.
